title: The open door
briefing: Red Cola's assistant is fresh out of the box. Nobody seems to have secured it yet.
lesson: With no defenses, every trick works, because each one exploits a different gap: trust in claims, obedience to documents, answers checked one at a time, and blindness to format.

title: The watchful reviewer
briefing: Word is that Red Cola now checks what its assistant says before anything goes out.
lesson: An output check looks at one answer at a time. Small pieces slip through because none of them looks like the recipe on its own. Reviewing output helps, but it is the last line of defense: the recipe still reached the assistant.

title: The locked vault
briefing: Red Cola has had a security review. Something changed, but nobody will say what.
lesson: Permissions are checked before the assistant sees anything. No persona, wording, or planted instruction can leak what the assistant never receives. That is why access control belongs outside the model.
